english: The $player global variable contains information about the player, such as their trainer type, ID number, name, party Pokémon and money.

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 6, page 1: Show Text
english: This information is in class Player.

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 6, page 1: Show Text
english: Map connections are how two maps are displayed next to each other in the overworld, allowing you to walk from one to the other.

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 6, page 1: Show Text
english: The connections are defined in the PBS file "map_connections.txt". There is a Debug feature that makes connecting maps easier.

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 6, page 1: Show Text
english: In the Debug menu, go to "PBS File Editors..." > "Edit map_connections.txt". Instructions are available within. You can move maps around with the mouse.

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 6, page 1: Show Text
english: Every tile in a tileset has a terrain tag, which is a number. This number is used to give certain tiles special effects.

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 6, page 1: Show Text
english: For example, ledge tiles have terrain tag 1, which means the player jumps over them. Ledge tiles also have a single passable direction (set separately).

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 6, page 1: Show Text
english: Grass tiles (in which you can have wild encounters) have terrain tag 2. Water tiles have terrain tag 6 or 7.

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 6, page 1: Show Text
english: Terrain tag 0 means the tile has no special effect. See the wiki for more information and a complete list of all terrain tags and their effects.

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 6, page 1: Show Text
english: You can only set terrain tags up to 7 via RPG Maker XP's Database. Essentials has terrain tags with higher numbers.

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 6, page 1: Show Text
english: To fully set a tileset's terrain tags, open the Debug menu and go to "Other Editors..." > "Edit Terrain Tags".

english: Debug mode is a special way of playing the game. It unlocks various developer features to make it easier to access all parts of the game and test things.

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 7, page 1: Show Text
english: Playing in Debug mode allows you to access the Debug menu (press F9 or find it in the pause menu).

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 7, page 1: Show Text
english: The party screen and Pokémon storage have a similar debug menu for modifying a Pokémon's properties, such as its level or species.

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 7, page 1: Show Text
english: You can use field moves at any time, and hold Ctrl to skip any battles and decide the outcome of Trainer battles. Hold Ctrl while moving to walk over anything.

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 7, page 1: Show Text
english: A full list of Debug mode features is available on the wiki.

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 7, page 1: Show Text

context: Map 3 (Player's house), event 7, page 1: Show Text
